results.title: FigCraft guide, the free Figma alternative written in Rust
results.content:
FigCraft is a free Figma alternative, open source and written in Rust, for designing interfaces and prototypes offline on macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD and in the browser. The official repository went up on October 9, 2026 and counts 2,558 GitHub stars as of October 18. The project calls itself alpha. Drawing screens with components and auto layout already works; properly opening the .fig files that arrive from a client does not, not yet.

Update, 25 October 2026

Update, 23 October 2026

Update, 18 October 2026

FigCraft, a free Figma alternative in Rust, with three screens of a mobile app on the canvas, the layers panel on the left and the Design panel with auto layout on the right [...] Figma, for anyone who doesn't use it, is the reference program for interface design (UI, meaning the screens, buttons and menus of an app or a site; the difference from UX is explained in the guide to UX and UI). The Starter plan is free but limited, while the Professional plan costs $16 a month per full seat, rising to $55 on the Organization plan and $90 on Enterprise, according to the official price list. FigCraft costs nothing, asks for no account, sends no telemetry, saves work to .figcraft archives on disk. The license is dual (MIT or Apache-2.0, take your pick) and allows commercial use. [...] The pace is typical of the family. Six versions shipped in five days, from 0.2.0 on October 10 to 0.6.0 on the 14th. As of October 18 the releases have passed 250,000 downloads in total. The most downloaded file of 0.5.1 is still the 64-bit Windows installer (32,704 downloads), ahead of the Mac image (13,926). The repository carries dedicated instructions for AI agents (the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files), but the latest fixes also credit outside developers, a sign that a small community has already formed around the project.

For magazines, books and brochures the suite also has an InDesign clone, which we tested on a Mac in our guide to DesignCraft, the free InDesign alternative.

This is the big ace up the FigCraft sleeve. Being a free Figma alternative changes the math for anyone paying out of their own pocket. With no subscription in a foreign currency, the budget becomes more predictable, and the month ends with fewer surprises.

Figma also has a free plan, but with limits that show up as your work grows. The paid plans unlock more features, and the price weighs on anyone earning in Brazilian reais.

One word of caution, though. Free projects can change their model over time, either by creating paid plans or by limiting features. So read the current terms of use carefully. Knowing what is available today helps you plan without surprises tomorrow.
